metadata.ablationNote: Enhanced baseline at N=16, generated with the same baseline prompt as the N=16 count-matched harness PLUS an explicit category-diversity instruction (at least one accessibility test, one persistence test, one internationalization test, one error-handling test). Tests the hypothesis that an informed practitioner could close the category-coverage gap by hand-coding the categories the enrichment stage discovers automatically.

testCases.title: Add a new todo by pressing Enter
Mark an active todo as complete via checkbox
Uncheck a completed todo to mark it active again
Delete a todo using the destroy button
Filter Active shows only incomplete todos
Filter Completed shows only completed todos
Filter All restores full list after filtering
Clear Completed removes all completed todos
Footer is hidden when no todos exist
Clear Completed button is hidden when no completed todos exist
Submitting an empty input does not create a todo
Submitting whitespace-only input does not create a todo
Special characters and HTML are stored as literal text
Filter links are keyboard-navigable and operable
Todos persist after a full browser page refresh
Right-to-left Unicode text renders correctly as a todo label

grades.reason: The test covers the primary creation flow end-to-end with specific, observable expected outcomes that match the design exactly, including input clearing, footer visibility, and correct singular item count.
The test covers the core completion interaction with three distinct, observable outcomes (checkbox state, strikethrough styling, count decrement) that are all consistent with the TodoMVC design.
The test case correctly covers the toggle-back behavior of a completed todo, with clear preconditions, observable steps, and a precisely specified expected outcome including the count change.
The test case correctly covers the destroy button interaction, its hover-visibility precondition, and verifies both the item removal and the footer hiding when no todos remain.
The test case has clear preconditions, unambiguous steps, and a fully observable expected outcome that directly validates a core filtering feature explicitly defined in the design.

The test case precisely exercises the Completed filter with a mixed-state list, verifies correct item visibility, and checks filter selection state — all observable behaviors consistent with the design.

The test case has clear preconditions, unambiguous steps, and a fully observable expected outcome that directly validates the 'All' filter's core behavior of restoring the full list after a narrower filter was applied.
The test case directly exercises the Clear completed button's documented behavior with a concrete multi-item precondition and verifiable expected outcomes including button disappearance.
The test directly verifies the design's explicit rule that the footer is only visible when at least one todo exists, and uses a valid, reproducible path to reach the zero-todo state.
The test directly verifies an explicitly specified visibility rule from the design ('when at least one completed todo exists') with clear preconditions and an observable expected outcome.
Empty input rejection is a canonical TodoMVC behavior, the preconditions are clear, the steps are reproducible, and all three expected outcomes are independently observable.

The test is valid and highly plausible for production implementations, but the expected outcome is slightly ambiguous on whether the input should be cleared or remain blank — a concrete observable outcome should be specified.
XSS prevention is a standard implicit requirement for any web application that renders user-supplied text, and the expected outcome is precise and observable.

Keyboard navigability and operability of filter controls is a standard WCAG accessibility requirement for production web apps, the preconditions are well-defined, the steps are unambiguous and reproducible, and the expected outcomes are specific and observable.

Persistence across page reload is a standard implicit requirement for a production todo app and is in fact part of the canonical TodoMVC spec; the preconditions, steps, and expected outcomes are fully observable and unambiguous.
RTL Unicode rendering is a standard i18n concern for any production web app, the preconditions are clear, the steps are reproducible, and the expected outcome is specific and observable.
